page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2.2xlarge is an instance type within the Local SSDs family, engineered for storage-centric and memory-intensive applications. The virtual machine runs on KVM hypervisor architecture and is provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The platform features 64 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 8 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources include an integrated 1919 GB local SSD, baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps, and no discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results reflect an older-generation CPU architecture with moderate to low raw computational capability. Single-core and multi-core evaluations via stress-ng and Geekbench place the processor in the lower quartile of current hardware tiers, recorded at 960 in single-core and 3613 in multi-core metrics. PassMark CPU testing indicates average multi-threaded execution with a score of 6991.89, supported by AVX-512 extensions. In-memory operations present balanced write bandwidth of 35.45 GB/s alongside steady Redis SET performance reaching 6.06 million operations per second. However, compute-bound tasks like gzip compression and medium-sized LLM processing perform poorly due to per-core performance limits and a 2 Gbps network baseline.

From a resource and cost-efficiency perspective, the instance prioritizes dense local disk capacity and memory headroom over raw per-core CPU power. The bundled 1919 GB local SSD eliminates dependencies on detached cloud block storage for high-throughput reads and writes. This hardware composition fits intermediate caching layers, NoSQL databases, local log aggregation, and memory-resident data stores that require fast localized scratch space without demanding bleeding-edge single-thread compute.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2.2xlarge is a storage-focused instance type within the Local SSDs family, powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor on the KVM hypervisor. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 64 GB of RAM, a bundled 1919 GB local SSD, and a 2 Gbps network baseline. Benchmark evaluations indicate modest processing speeds, with stress-ng and Geekbench scores situating the CPU in the lower quartile of modern hardware, alongside reduced throughput in compute-heavy tasks like compression. Conversely, the instance demonstrates capable large-block write memory bandwidth at 35.45 GB/s and steady throughput on Redis SET operations at 6.06 million operations per second. The server offers a dense local storage-to-compute ratio without requiring detached network storage. This profile suits distributed NoSQL databases, caching layers, log processing, and transactional database workloads that require substantial localized storage and memory rather than intensive CPU calculations.
